claims.text: The baseline TiVNbTa alloy has a single-phase BCC dendritic microstructure.
The baseline TiVNbTa alloy has a room-temperature yield strength of about 800 MPa.
The baseline TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of 330 MPa at 1273 K under the stated 30% strain regime.
The baseline TiVNbTa alloy has a compressive strength of 423 MPa at 1273 K under the stated 30% strain regime.
Adding tungsten to TiVNbTa will improve its high-temperature yield strength.
Adding tungsten to TiVNbTa will improve its high-temperature compressive strength.
The strength improvement will make the alloy more compatible for use as an intermediate layer between W and CuCrZr.
Vacuum arc melting will ensure homogeneous incorporation of tungsten.
The selected tungsten addition and processing route will retain the single-phase BCC dendritic microstructure.
Tungsten addition will enhance lattice distortion within the BCC phase.
Tungsten addition will enhance refractory bonding characteristics within the BCC phase.
Tungsten increases lattice friction in the TiVNbTa-based BCC phase.
The tungsten-induced lattice effects hinder dislocation motion at elevated temperature.
Hindered dislocation motion causes improved retention of strength at elevated temperature.
Tungsten can provide the proposed strengthening without disrupting the single-phase BCC structure.
At 1273 K under comparable loading, the modified alloy will have a yield strength greater than 330 MPa.
At 1273 K under comparable loading, the modified alloy will have a compressive strength greater than 423 MPa.
Maintaining a single-phase BCC structure is critical for the intended plasma-facing and heat-transfer application.
